label: early original-phase steps (t=2-4) after a g in the first two positions
explanation: Fires during the original phase at steps 2-4 when the sequence starts with g (first_tok=g carries 91% of mass, lift 23x), and also at step 3 when g is the second token. Activations are strongest when the sequence starts g g (top examples all begin g g, peaking at t=3 near the max), and weaker when only one g leads. The input token at the firing step does not matter. Never fires at t=0-1, almost never at t>=5, and is essentially silent in the delimiter and copy phases (under 1% of mass, mostly at the delimiter when the first output is g). A g later in the sequence does not trigger it. Dev F1 0.89, mass recall 0.97.

issues: I reproduced the reported test scores exactly: P 0.866, R 0.909, F1 0.887, mass recall 0.965.

The core claims hold. On dev, first_tok=g at t=2 and at t=3 each have precision 1.0, with 27% and 47% of the mass. first_tok=g carries 91% of the mass. Activation is zero at t=0-1. The delimiter phase has 0.6% of the mass and the copy phase 0.1%, and the delimiter activations are mostly where out_tok=g. A g at position 2 does not trigger the feature: orig(2)=g at t=4-5 has precision 0.05. Every top example starts with 'g g' and peaks at t=3.

The 'g is the second token' branch is weak and unreliable. orig(1)=g with first_tok!=g at t=3 has dev precision 0.61 and only 7% of the mass, and that branch causes most of the false positives (about 6k on dev). The same case at t=4 fires 26% of the time and is not covered (5.9% recall, 1.6% mass). I found no token pattern that explains when this branch fires.
first_tok=g at t=4 with no second g has precision 0.83, which accounts for roughly 2.3k false positives. At t=4 the 'g g' case fires reliably (precision 1.0).

There is a small systematic miss: in sequences starting 'g g', the feature also fires at t=5 (precision 0.998, but only 0.8% of the mass). Adding this term only moves dev F1 from 0.887 to 0.891, which I count as negligible.
Minor nuance on 'strongest when the sequence starts g g': in 'g g' sequences the activation at t=2 is actually weak (about 0.1 of max). The peak is at t=3-4.

The label slightly overclaims by putting 'a g in the first two positions' on equal footing. The first position does almost all the work; a g in the second position only partially triggers the feature.
